title: Annotatio IV §.IX: Augustine (4) — exclude local presence and oral handling; body in one place
pass_a_gloss: And that (4.) with exclusion of local presence and oral participation: For so he proceeds in Tract. 30 on John: Until the age is finished, the Lord is above, yet nonetheless here also with us is the Truth of the Lord. FOR THE BODY OF THE LORD, IN WHICH HE ROSE, ought to be IN ONE PLACE, but His truth is diffused everywhere. And Tract. 50 on John: Christ even when absent is present: For He has brought His body into heaven, He has not withdrawn His Majesty from the world. And Tract. I on the Epistle of John: We cannot handle with HAND (mouth) the Lord now sitting in heaven, but touch by Faith.
pass_b_english: Augustine (4): local presence and oral handling shut out — until the age ends the Lord is above, yet His Truth is here with us.

The Lord’s risen body must be in ONE PLACE; His truth is everywhere. Absent yet present: body in heaven, Majesty not withdrawn. We cannot handle Him in heaven with hand or mouth — only touch by Faith.
source_text: Idque (4.) cum exclusione præsentiæ localis & participationis oralis: Ita enim Tract. 30. in Johannem pergit: Donec seculum finiatur, sursum est Dominus, sed tamen, hic etiam nobiscum est Veritas Domini. CORPUS ENIM DOMINI, IN QUO RESURREXIT, UNO LOCO esse oportet, veritas autem ejus ubique diffusa est. Et Tract. 50. in Johann. Christus absens etiam præsens est: Corpus enim suum intulit cœlo, Majestatem non abstulit mundo. Et Tract. I. in Epistolam Johannis. Dominum jam in cælo sedentem MANU (ore) contrectare non possumus, sed Fide contingere.

lemmas.gloss: ought to be in ONE PLACE

notes: Augustine (4): one place; faith not mouth.
